successors.name: County of Foix
successors.text: the Dordogne, Corrèze and Haute-Vienne cells of Cliopatria's last shape, which the county-of-foix dossier has joining the Albret composite

ledger.x: 1206: the County of Périgord, with its seat at Périgueux, is the earliest year of Cliopatria's shape.
October 1360: Périgord is ceded to Edward III by the Treaty of Brétigny.
1369: war resumes over the Brétigny lands.
1378: the French have retaken most of the ceded lands.
1378: Périgord returns to the French side with the reconquest of the ceded lands (see the contest above); the duchy-of-aquitaine dossier has the English loss of the Brétigny lands in 1377.
1398: the county is absorbed into the Kingdom of France: 'Périgord was eventually absorbed into the Kingdom of France in 1398.'
1400: the crown's prince Louis of Orléans becomes Count of Périgord ('Périgord (1400–1407)', infobox 'Count of Périgord | 1400–1407').
1400: the House of Orléans takes the county; same state, same colour.

wars.name: Hundred Years' War in Périgord
wars.outcome: Périgord was ceded to England in 1360, the war resumed in 1369, the French retook most ceded lands by 1378, and the war ended at Castillon on 17 July 1453.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey on the pages opened; the Brétigny cession of 1360 lists regions, not lines.
